problems.title: The same metric, calculated differently
problems.body: Report A and report B disagree because each re-implements the rule. Clearline compiles the "trusted dataset" rule once and every metric, extract and view uses it.

problems.title: Transformations nobody can explain
problems.body: Business rules live in a versioned data contract and run as whitelisted operations, so a result can be traced to the rule and the version that produced it.

problems.title: Quality problems found after reporting
problems.body: Rows are validated before they count. Failures are quarantined with the rule and source row, and a failing reconciliation check marks the batch untrusted.

problems.title: Queries recreated by hand
problems.body: Saved queries are versioned, parameterized and re-validated for whoever runs them.

problems.title: Analyses that depend on a person remembering
problems.body: Durable schedules run in the worker without any client, with recorded runs, retries and delivery attempts.

problems.title: Alerts without evidence
problems.body: Each analysis states its method, inputs, quality measures and limitations. Findings are statistical deviations, not claimed causes.

problems.title: Sensitive data leaking through side doors
problems.body: One field-policy resolver redacts every surface, and permissions are re-checked when scheduled work runs and before delivery.

problems.title: Failures that cannot be diagnosed
problems.body: Attempts, outcomes, checks, runs and deliveries are recorded and linked by correlation id in an append-only audit trail.

limitations: All data is synthetic. Nothing here has run in production, and no uptime, scale or compliance claim is made, including HIPAA.
No SSO or MFA, no API rate limiting (the public assistant has its own limiter), no field encryption, no service identities for schedules.
Benchmarks come from one 4-vCPU machine without a GPU; behaviour beyond 100,000 rows per batch, multiple API instances and multi-day operation is unmeasured.
The live Claude provider path was not verified in the recorded results, and the optional insight narrator was tested with a stub only.
Email and webhooks were tested against local receivers, not real relays or remote endpoints.
macOS and Windows builds of the native client, and GPU rendering, are unverified.
Alerting rules, dashboards in a monitoring system, automated backups and infrastructure as code are not shipped.
Test evidence was recorded at commit dc06c95. Later changes (the web client, the assistant) have their own, smaller evidence as stated on each capability.
scenarios: 1,000 claims become a trusted batch with 9 passing reconciliation checks; the reported total equals the generator's ground truth; lineage runs from source row to export.
An identical resubmission has no effect; five concurrent duplicates produce one batch.
11 rows quarantined with exact rule and row; reject rate 5.45% exceeds 5%, so the batch is untrusted and excluded from trusted metrics.
A process killed mid-transaction leaves nothing visible and recovers on restart.
Cross-tenant reads and sensitive exports are refused and audited at the API and SQL layers.
Loss in transit and out-of-band drift are detected and explained; metrics are qualified; trust is restored after repair.
14 metrics equal hand-written SQL, generator truth and the native client for both tenants.
A question becomes a validated proposal; nothing runs until asked; hostile model output is never executed.
24 inference attacks are rejected; with the validator bypassed the database still refuses.
A due-time run happens exactly once with two racing schedulers; DST gaps and overlaps behave as documented.
Email, signed webhooks, retries and exports; a field made sensitive after the query blocks delivery.
A planted anomaly is ranked first by both algorithms with observed value equal to ground truth; seeded outliers ranked 1 to 3.
Save, schedule, anomaly, insight, notification; revoke the identity and the pending delivery is blocked.
